mechanism: Ginkgo biloba may inhibit monoamine oxidase (MAO) activity while isoniazid is a known MAO inhibitor, potentially potentiating MAO inhibition effects and increasing risk of hypertensive crisis and serotonin-related adverse effects.
action: Monitor blood pressure and counsel patients on avoiding tyramine-rich foods; consider discontinuing ginkgo biloba during isoniazid therapy or use with caution under clinical supervision.
